payload.raw: Deployment and Security
This guide covers a production deployment pattern for StreamMDX with strict CSP, hosted worker assets, and controlled HTML rendering.

inline.text: This guide covers a production deployment pattern for StreamMDX with strict CSP, hosted worker assets, and controlled HTML rendering.

payload.raw: Recommended production topology

1. Build your app and StreamMDX worker bundle in CI.
2. Copy `markdown-worker.js` into static assets.
3. Serve docs/app pages and worker from the same origin.
4. Keep CSP strict (`worker-src 'self'`) and avoid `blob:`.

payload.raw: CSP baseline
A conservative baseline for most deployments:

inline.text: A conservative baseline for most deployments:

payload.highlightedHtml:
default-src 'self';
script-src 'self';
style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
img-src 'self' data: https:;
worker-src 'self';
connect-src 'self' https:;

payload.raw: Notes:

- `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is often needed for runtime style injection in UI stacks.
- If your stack supports nonce-based styles, prefer nonce over unrestricted inline styles.

payload.raw: HTML rendering policy
StreamMDX applies sanitization for untrusted HTML by default. Keep that enabled unless your input source is fully trusted and audited.

inline.text: StreamMDX applies sanitization for untrusted HTML by default. Keep that enabled unless your input source is fully trusted and audited.

payload.raw: Operational policy:

- Enable `features.html` only when required.
- Prefer render-layer overrides (`htmlElements`) over sanitizer allowlist expansion.
- Review any allowlist changes as security-sensitive changes.

payload.raw: Code-row HTML emitted by the syntax highlighter (per-line `span.line` markup with Shiki theme variables) uses one shared allowlist on every runtime: `pre`/`code`/`span`/`div`/`br` with `class`, `data-*`, and `style` attributes. The browser path runs that allowlist through DOMPurify; the Node/SSR path (snapshot prerender, `MarkdownBlocksRenderer`) runs it through the DOM-free rehype pipeline, so no `window`/jsdom shim is required. Surviving style declarations must use an allowed presentational property (theme foreground/background colors, font emphasis, `--shiki-*` variables) and an ASCII value from a conservative charset, so CSS backslash escapes, comment-splitting tricks, and function values such as `url(...)`/`expression(...)` are dropped on both paths while theme foreground colors and CSS variables are preserved. Tags whose content is never unwrapped (`svg`, `template`, `iframe`, `math`, `thead`, `title`, …) follow DOMPurify's forbidden-contents set on both paths, so an `<svg><text>…</text></svg>` subtree disappears identically in the browser and during prerender, while other disallowed tags (for example `em` or a stray `textarea`) are unwrapped and keep their text on both paths.

payload.raw: MDX policy

MDX execution is opt-in. `contentPolicy` defaults to `"restricted"` and does not evaluate authored expressions. Register fixed native source components with `defineContentComponent` in `contentComponents`; the worker receives only names and render conditions, while validators and component callbacks remain on the host. Native projected children are separate React nodes. This registry is inactive under `"markdown"` and `"trusted-mdx"`.

payload.raw: Full MDX requires an explicit `createTrustedMdxEngine` from `@stream-mdx/react/trusted-mdx`, passed with `contentPolicy="trusted-mdx"` and `engines.mdx`. The host import map grants explicit module bindings only; unresolved imports are not fetched. Evaluation runs authored code in the host realm, requires `unsafe-eval` in `script-src`, and is not a sandbox. Use it only for trusted, reviewed content. For user-generated input, keep the restricted policy and leave `engines.mdx` unset.

payload.raw: Native worker `FINALIZED` reports native semantic completion, not trusted compilation or host render readiness. The trusted document distinguishes requested, projected, and actually rendered revisions; lease/request/engine checks reject stale work before evaluation. A failed render may restore prior committed UI, but cannot undo side effects from code that already executed.

payload.raw: Agent content and code renderers

For agent or user content, disable raw HTML unless needed and keep full MDX evaluation off. Set `features.mdx: false` if the feed does not need component syntax. Enable `linkSafety` for links rendered by StreamMDX; it does not control navigation from custom renderers.

payload.raw: Replacing and customizing codeRenderers

StreamMDX engine-v2 allows granular code fence renderer customization via the `codeRenderers` prop. You can map specific fence languages to specialized renderers while letting standard code blocks use the default highlighter:

inline.text: StreamMDX engine-v2 allows granular code fence renderer customization via the
prop. You can map specific fence languages to specialized renderers while letting standard code blocks use the default highlighter:

payload.highlightedHtml:
import { StreamingMarkdown, type CodeFenceRenderer } from "@stream-mdx/react";
import { MermaidBlock } from "@stream-mdx/mermaid";

const CustomMetricRenderer: CodeFenceRenderer = ({ code, language, isFinalized, renderCode }) => {
  try {
    const data = JSON.parse(code);
    return (
      <div className="metric-panel">
        <span className="badge">{isFinalized ? "Finalized" : "Streaming..."}</span>
        <pre>{JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)}</pre>
      </div>
    );
  } catch {
    return <>{renderCode}</>;
  }
};

export function AgentChatStream({ text }: { text: string }) {
  return (
    <StreamingMarkdown
      text={text}
      engine="worker" // or "main-thread"
      features={{ mdx: false, html: false, tables: true, math: true }}
      linkSafety={{ enabled: true }}
      codeRenderers={{
        mermaid: MermaidBlock,
        metric: CustomMetricRenderer,
      }}
    />
  );
}

payload.raw: Incident response quick path
If a production issue appears in rendered output:

inline.text: If a production issue appears in rendered output:

payload.raw:
1. Disable risky feature flag (`html` or `mdx`) first.
2. Roll back to previous worker bundle + app release.
3. Compare regression snapshots to isolate the rendering delta.
4. Patch and redeploy with a new snapshot/perf report.
